data.name: Stratside
data.detailed_description:
Intro & Gameplay


Stratside is a Puzzle Defense game where you save planets from an enemy who changes the direction of gravity! Place gadgets to attack the intruder! Each gadget uses a custom attack pattern: combine your resources strategically to defeat the enemy before he reaches his goal! Don't let him press the red button, or a whole planet will be destroyed!

The enemy can run, jump and change the gravity direction with multiple rituals. He reacts to your placements, and uses his virtuous mind to select the safest path! He will surprise you with unexpected alternative routes, and you will need to use logic to catch him: it's ambush time!

You can preview the enemy path in real-time thanks to a hologram of the intruder, and change placements as many times as wanted, without annoying time limits. When you feel ready, invoke the enemy and enjoy the show: if your placements are perfect, the gadgets will stop him! Spoiler: someone's robotic head may end up ejected.

Features


The innovative gameplay of Stratside comes together with tons of engaging content:

  • 12+ amusing gadgets, to attack the enemy in brain-twisting ways.
  • Obstacles that affect how the enemy can move through the level.
  • Movable blocks, to create new surfaces where gadgets and obstacles can be placed.
  • Levels with multiple portals and red buttons, that increase the number of possible paths for the enemy in challenging ways.
  • 100+ levels: many planets to be saved!
  • Level Editor to create your own levels: from tiny to giant, options are almost endless!
  • Steam Workshop, to play levels made by the community and share your creations!
  • Level Manager, a file browser-like UI created specifically for the game, so that you can organize your levels in level sets.
  • Tutorials that you can follow or skip.
  • Customizable Music: you can select the playing frequency for every music type to match your tastes, from epic space tracks to relaxing piano music, among many others: there are 80+ music tracks.
  • Customizable Art: planets are like colors; you like this one and I like that one... so you can change the frequency of each celestial body if you want! The same applies to galaxies!
  • Settings, many settings: controls, video, audio, gameplay, user interface and more.
  • Full gamepad support, and the same goes for mouse and keyboard, of course.
  • Optimized enemy artificial intelligence that finds optimal paths in milliseconds, even in giant levels!
  • Steam Cloud to sync progress across devices if you want.
  • Steam Achievements.
  • Steam Trading Cards.

Compared to other games


Stratside is a puzzle game where you control a cursor and place objects in a level, while the AI-controlled character moves in a side-scrolling environment. You might have seen that in save-them-all games like Lemmings, Flockers or Mario vs Donkey Kong. In those titles, you help friendly unintelligent characters to build paths and reach a goal, while in Stratside you prevent a much more clever character (the enemy) from reaching his objective.

Stratside is also a defense game, but whilst traditional defense games feature a large number of dummy enemies with predictable paths, Stratside's smarter enemy is much harder to catch, and powerful enough to move colossal planets through space! Unlike many defense games, Stratside does not make you click on gadgets in real-time to make them attack, here they are auto-battlers! In Stratside, the gameplay magic is in the placement phase!


Stratside was created with the motivation of making a game with a unique, innovative gameplay, probably quite different to anything you have played before, that hopefully you will enjoy playing!

If you like the game, consider buying it or adding it to your wishlist, and share this page with your friends!

data.short_description: Stratside is a Puzzle Defense game where you save planets from a gravity-changing enemy! Place gadgets to attack the intruder! Combine your resources strategically to defeat the enemy before he reaches his goal! DON'T let him press the red button! This game is like the opposite of Lemmings!

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7
  • Processador: Intel i3 or AMD Ryzen 3
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Nvidia GeForce GT 630 or equivalent*
  • DirectX: Versão 11
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 2 GB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: *Some older GPUs (such as Nvidia GeForce 315) can run the game but with issues (due to outdated drivers). If you have such an old GPU you may want to check if you can run the demo first.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Sistema Operativo: Windows 10
  • Processador: Intel i5 or AMD Ryzen 5
  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Nvidia GeForce GTX 760 or equivalent
  • DirectX: Versão 12
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 2 GB de espaço livre

reviews.review:
first things first: yes, [b]stratside[/b] is a particularly ugly game, and that's coming from someone who doesn't care about graphics, even less so in puzzle games. it's also clunkier and less polished than it should be, especially at this price, almost matches the quality of the graphics. unfortunately, it's unlikely that anything will change, but the concept and the game itself is still fun for the most part.

it's [b]tower defense without the fast pace and frantic clicking[/b], ideal for me. the goal is to place various gadgets around the level that will hurt and eventually stop a single enemy from reaching the button and destroying the planet in the background. yes, [b]only one enemy, but it's pretty smart[/b], always knows what to do and where to go, it can even switch gravity, walk on the side of blocks, jump around, etc.

however, instead of quickly placing turrets and whatnot on the go, you can [b]preview enemy movement via a hologram[/b] (or tiles on the level lighting up), [b]adjust gadgets accordingly[/b] to outsmart the ai in advance, then [b]press the invoke button when everything's in place[/b]. it turns green when you're ready to cause as much damage as the enemy's hp, no point in pressing it before that. the alien's [b]hologram keeps running the level over and over[/b], always adapting to the current situaton, which is pretty handy, but sadly, [b]there are no hologram controls[/b], can't pause or rewind and sometimes have to wait until it reaches the button before it starts over so you can see what your changes caused.

there are [b]120 levels[/b], only one unlocked at a time, [b]no timer or other limits[/b], except of course the arsenal available for the current level. there are [b]about 12 gadgets[/b] introduced as you keep playing. mines trigger when stepped on, the big hand slaps the alien if it stands next to it, the flamethrower hurts it from 2 blocks away, and there are others with bigger distances, some even go through walls or attack diagonally, etc. the problem is [b]the currently held item is not visible, only an empty cursor[/b], so you have to constantly monitor the numbers in the top left to see if you put back all the removed items and not holding one without realizing it.

[b]tutorials[/b] are available before certain levels and they can be checked again in the main menu, but [b]the tutorial menu only  appears after completing level 1[/b], which is just as unintuitive as dumping 11 (ELEVEN!) screens' worth of tutorials on the player before starting the very first level that only involves placing a single item.

[b]there are a billion settings available[/b], basic stuff like windowed mode, resolutions, separate volume sliders (though ui sounds can't be muted without muting the entire game, 'sound effects' don't cover those for some reason, so can't have just music without the annyong clicking), there are also graphics settings like brightness, shadows, textures, anti-aliasing, etc. nothing will make the game look decent though. 

[b]controls are a bit unintuitive but rebindable[/b] and there are a lot of them, plus many other things to tinker with, some more useful than others, but it's mostly unnecessary. people won't know (or care) about most of them, a few could use a bit more explanation, and [b]settings aren't available while playing a level[/b], which is a huge bummer.

there are [b]two things I recommend changing in the settings:[/b] tick [i]'item auto-pick'[/i], so if you have more than one of the same gadget, you can place them quickly without selecting the same thing in the corner or with a hotkey again and again. the other is a keybind: [b]rotating a placed gadget is only possible with a hotkey[/b], another truly unintuitive thing, but binding it to the mousewheel/middle mouse button works well, even though left click should do it by default, it doesn't do anything in that situation (right click is for removal). don't forget to change [i]'pick item from selected supplier button'[/i] to something else, can be whatever, you'll either directly click items or press the numbers to select one.

while the graphics are subpar, [b]the music's pretty good and there are about 80(!) tracks covering 11 styles[/b] from rock to sci-fi, action to spooky, and you can set how often you want (or don't want) to hear each type. same goes for graphics, you can toggle background movement and how often should each planet and background type appear, though [b]planets themselves can't be turned off[/b] even by turning their probability to zero. sure, that's what the alien's about to destroy, but you won't waste time trying incomplete solutions until the game tells you it's all clear anyway, and [b]planets are a real eyesore as well, so I'd very much like to get rid of them[/b].

the game is [b]very much a mixed bag[/b]: the concept is great and it's mostly fun, but you often have to wrestle with the controls even after rebinding them. there is a level editor and workshop support and [b]mid-level saving[/b] (if you go back to a level, there will be a [i]'restore placements'[/i] button), also plenty of settings, but many of them are unnecessary while crucial ones are missing. music is nice and varied, graphics are bad, which will sadly turn most people off immediately.

there's a good amount of content and the potential for even more, but these days I wouldn't bank on too many puzzle games running away with workshop levels, so the bottom line is, [b]15 eur is way too much for something that needs this much polish and quality of life adjustments[/b], and since they're unlikely to happen anytime soon, if ever, [b]only pick it up on deep sale if you have a higher tolerance for jank and clunkiness[/b].
